A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MigGPT research. All 19 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original migration and retrieval experiments, CVE backporting results, ablations, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds model comparisons, compilation success measurements, and a timing comparison with human experts.

M1.justification: The CFP-based retrieval, alignment, and migration procedure is retained. Algorithms 1–2 move to Appendix D.4, and the prompt text is unchanged apart from renaming Namespace Prompt to Structure Prompt. New Algorithm 3 documents generation of the existing CFP component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported 135 migration examples from RT-PREEMPT, Raspberry Pi Linux, and HAOC across kernel versions 4.19, 5.4, 5.10, and 6.6, plus the 350-instance CVE benchmark. The additional measurements use retained tasks; proposed generalization to other domains is not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated OpenAI-o1 and DeepSeek-R1 comparators. Its CVE comparison replaces PATCH and SyDIT with TSBPORT and PPatHF while retaining FixMorph and the LLM comparisons. It also introduces human experts as timing comparators. DeepSeek-V2.5 results are retained in Appendix E.

E3.justification: v2 introduces containerized kernel-compilation testing and a timed comparison with three human experts, and evaluates an additional Llama-3.1-8B configuration. Existing match metrics, the CodeBLEU threshold of 0.9, and retry limit m = 3 remain unchanged. Human-review procedures are newly disclosed rather than demonstrably revised.

E4.justification: The module ablations, retry-limit sensitivity, line-edit failure analysis, challenge cases, and CodeBLEU-threshold analysis are retained. Appendix G.1 adds an illustrative explanation of traditional-method limitations, without reporting an additional tested failure case or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's multiple human reviewers describe adjudication procedures, without introducing statistical uncertainty or agreement estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds o1, R1, and 8B results, compilation rates, and expert timing results. Table 4 reports MigGPT compilation rates of 66.67% and 79.26% versus vanilla rates of 16.30% and 31.85%. FixMorph's CVE entry changes from 75% to 24.63%, without explanation; Llama-3.1-70B retrieval queries change from 1.24 to 1.29. Changed headline averages use a different model roster and do not establish a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The migration formulation, Type 1/Type 2 conditions, and line-edit-distance recurrence are unchanged, including their relocated appendix presentations. Algorithm 3 supplies implementation documentation rather than a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The benchmark, CFP, MigGPT, and superiority-over-vanilla claims remain. v2 adds the specific claim that MigGPT takes only 2.08% of human experts' average time and emphasizes the existing retrieval-plus-migration formulation as a distinction from prior approaches.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of structural refactoring difficulties for traditional tools, CFP versus intermediate representations, and possible extension to forked-code porting. It also attributes weaker 8B results to limited base-model capability. Existing challenge explanations, failure interpretations, and impact qualifications largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.4 newly specifies CFP tokenization, scope matching, function-call detection, and generation pseudocode. Appendices F.1–F.3 add hardware and operating-system details, human-review staffing and voting criteria, and compilation procedures. These substantially expand documentation of previously underspecified implementation and evaluation components.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to OpenAI-o1, DeepSeek-R1, KernelGPT, and BlockScope and removes the GNU Diffutils reference. Section 2.1 sharpens the contrast with FixMorph, TSBPORT, and PPatHF by emphasizing their assumed known target locations. The broader first-LLM-framework positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 trims Preliminaries into Problem Formulation, renames challenge and prompt terminology, and reorganizes algorithms, settings, additional results, and the impact statement into appendices. Introduction and related-work passages receive focused revisions, while most method explanations and the conclusion remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The two-column conference layout becomes a predominantly single-column preprint layout, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Tables 2–3 expand, DeepSeek-V2.5 results become separate appendix tables, and compilation/time tables, Algorithm 3, and Figure 16 are added. Existing analytical figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful operational validation through kernel compilation, broader comparisons, and substantially clearer CFP and human-evaluation documentation. These improve the paper's evidential support and inspectability. The gain is limited by the unexplained FixMorph score revision, sparse timing procedures, and new reporting errors: for example, Table 2's 76.25% Type 1 human-match average does not match its constituent rows.
